transcript:
User: We have a girl at the front desk, she picks up fine. Not sure why I'd need this.
Agent: Got it — if she’s picking up, that makes total sense. When she’s on the other line or steps away for lunch, what happens to the calls that come in?
User: We just call people back when Janet's busy or away. It's worked for us so far.
Agent: Makes sense — a lot of teams do that. What made you start looking into this right now—did something change?
User: Nothing's changed. Just curious about what you're offering, but not sure it's necessary for us right now.
Agent: Yeah, totally fair — if it’s working, no need to force a change. Just so I can tell if we’d even matter for you, what kind of business is it?
User: We're an auto body shop in Boston. Janet handles calls, and we've managed well enough without extra help.
Agent: Got it — an auto body shop, and Janet’s basically the hub for the phones, with callbacks when she’s tied up. Roughly how many calls a week do you think end up going to voicemail or getting missed when she’s busy or away?
User: We never really counted misses. Janet's been here 9 years and handles things, so it's not a big issue.
Agent: Totally — if Janet’s that solid, it won’t feel like a big issue day to day. When a new customer calls and it goes to voicemail, do you feel like you usually reach them before they call another shop, or do some just disappear?
User: We usually call back, but some might disappear. Not sure how often, though. Never really tracked it closely.
Agent: Yeah — that “some disappear” is usually the part that’s invisible until you track it. After you close, what happens to calls that come in at night or on weekends?
User: We just have a voicemail. People leave messages, and we get back to them during business hours.
Agent: Got it — so after-hours it’s voicemail, then you return them next day. When you do call those messages back, do you usually end up booking the estimate, or do you run into a lot of “already handled it”/no answer?
User: Mostly we book them, but sometimes they’ve already moved on or don’t pick up.
Agent: Yeah, that’s the tough part—by the time you call back, they’ve cooled off or already booked somewhere else. Mind if I do a quick 30‑second calculation to see what that might be costing you?
User: I suppose, but I still think we're doing fine. Go ahead, let's see what numbers you come up with.
Agent: Got it — and we’ll keep it conservative. So ballpark, how many calls a week do you think hit voicemail or get missed when Janet’s busy or away—10, 20, 30?
User: I'd say around 15 missed calls a week during busy hours.
Agent: Got it — 15 a week. Of those, what percent do you think would actually book an estimate or job if you answered live—like 30%, 50%, 70%?
User: Probably around 50% would book if we answered live.
Agent: Makes sense. And what’s your average ticket value—are we talking more like $500, $1,000, $2,000?
User: Our average ticket is about $1,100, but that's just an estimate.
Agent: Got it. If you booked even 50% of those 15 missed calls, that’s about **$8250 extra a week**—and that’s just one week, about **$35700/mo** over a month… does that feel directionally right to you?
User: Alright, as a backup layer I can see it. Let's book your demo and talk more.
Agent: Got it — glad it clicks as a backup layer. What’s your first name?
User: It's Dave. Let's set up this demo and see how it might fit in with what we're doing.
Agent: Got it, Dave. What’s your last name?
User: Kowalski, same as the shop. Let's get this demo on the calendar and see what you have to offer.
Agent: Thanks — and what’s the name of the shop?
User: It's Kowalski Auto Body. Let's get this demo scheduled to see if it can help us out.
Agent: Perfect, thanks. And… is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you?
User: Yes, this is the best number to reach me. Looking forward to the demo.
Agent: Perfect — thanks. And which time zone are you in: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: We're in Eastern Time, here in Boston, MA.
Agent: Got it — Eastern time. Perfect. So I have Dave Kowalski with Kowalski Auto Body, a contact number on file, and Eastern time — is that all correct?
User: Yes, that's correct. Looking forward to the demo. Let's see what you've got.
Agent: One moment while I check availability. Would you prefer later today or tomorrow for the demo?
User: Tomorrow would be better. Let me know what times you have available.
Agent: I can get you in as soon as **5:00 PM** or **5:45 PM** Eastern time tomorrow— which works?
User: 5:45 PM works for me. Let's go ahead and schedule it for then. Thanks.
Agent: So that’s **tomorrow (Thu, Aug 27) at 5:45 PM Eastern**, correct?
User: Yes, tomorrow at 5:45 PM Eastern sounds perfect. Looking forward to it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, Dave — you’re all set for **tomorrow at 5:45 PM Eastern**. You’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details so you can add it to your calendar (or reschedule if you need to).  

Is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Sure, take your time. Just let me know once it's confirmed. Thanks.
Agent: It’s confirmed, Dave — you’re set for tomorrow at 5:45 PM Eastern, and that SMS confirmation will come through shortly. Really glad you called; Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great rest of your day. Bye!
